adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at the diff for larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens() which, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, returns a response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. This sync endpoint is documented to return only access_token and expiry (per parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts's minimumTokenResponseSchema). However, the Lark code then calls `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)` which expects Lark's specific response format with `{ code, data: { refresh_token, refresh_expires_in, ... } }`. The sync response won't have this structure, causing the handler to fail or return undefined data. Unlike other integrations (Google, Office365, Zoom) that use parseRefreshTokenResponse to handle the sync case, Lark doesn't use this helper and directly processes the response expecting Lark's format.
